citations.claim: The DTV is a 5-year multiple-entry visa allowing 180 days per entry, extendable once per entry for an additional 180 days (up to 360 continuous days).
citations.placement: quote (inline, section 'What the DTV offers instead')
citations.verbatim: five-year validity, multiple entry, 180 days per entry, extendable once per entry for an additional 180 days

citations.claim: Muay Thai is an officially recognized Soft Power qualifying activity for the DTV, alongside Thai cooking courses, sports training, medical treatment, seminars, and cultural festivals.
Muay Thai is part of Thailand's official National Soft Power Strategy (THACCA), not only a DTV-qualifying activity.
citations.source: Muay Thai Visa Thailand (Kru Chart), soft power and the DTV
citations.notes: Source is a competitor gym's own promotional content (named author with SAT/MOE credentials per docs/seo-context.md gap analysis). Used only for the general Soft Power strategy claim, not for any Wildcat-specific comparison.

citations.claim: In 2025, general Thai language schools were removed from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' DTV Soft Power qualifying list; applicants wanting to study Thai are now directed to the Non-Immigrant ED visa instead. Muay Thai was not affected.
citations.source: The Thaiger, DTV guide (citing the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
citations.placement: quote (inline, section 'Where Muay Thai actually fits in this decision') + sources-block
citations.verbatim: Thai language schools were removed from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' qualifying soft power list
citations.notes: Cross-referenced against docs/dtv-fact-check.md item #15 (previously confirmed via The Thaiger + ExpatDen, consulted 2026-07-03). This fresh fetch (2026-08-06) confirms the fact-check's item #15 is still current. Non-negotiable brief instruction satisfied: never present language schools as a valid current DTV option.

citations.claim: The Non-Immigrant ED visa requires enrollment at a single accredited school or institution, with real attendance obligations, and a stay tied to a 90-day cycle with in-country 90-day reporting.
citations.source: Siam Legal, Thailand Education ED Visa
citations.verbatim: The holder of the ED visa is entitled to stay in Thailand for 90 days and can be extended for a period of one year from the date of first entry in Thailand. [...] Holders of the Non-Immigrant ED Visa must report their current address to a Thai immigration office every 90 days.

citations.claim: Leaving Thailand mid-cycle on the ED visa requires a re-entry permit first, or the visa lapses.
citations.source: Siam Legal, Thailand Education ED Visa

citations.claim: The Non-Immigrant ED visa is issued for education purposes only, with an initial 90-day validity from date of issuance.
citations.source: Royal Thai Embassy, Non-Immigrant Visa ED (Education)
citations.verbatim: ED Visa is valid for a single entry for education purposes only. [...] ED Visa is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance.

citations.claim: The DTV allows remote work for foreign employers only, not Thai employers or local clients; the ED visa does not permit work.
citations.placement: body prose (section 'What the DTV offers instead')
citations.notes: DTV work-rights confirmed directly ('Work rights: Foreign employers only'). The ED visa's lack of work authorization is deduced from its stated purpose ('education purposes only', Royal Thai Embassy) and is standard, uncontested practice; no single source states the negative explicitly, so the article avoids overclaiming and frames it structurally rather than as a cited legal prohibition.
